title: The ruler from Judah and the hope of the nations
source_text: Εἰ δὲ καὶ δευτέρας προφητείας ἐναργοῦς ἡμῖν εἶναι φαινομένης περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ χρεία ἐστὶν, ἐκθησόμεθα τὴν ἀναγραφεῖσαν πρὸ πλείστων ὅσων ἐτῶν τῆς Ἰησοῦ ἐπιδημίας ὑπὸ Μω(??)σέως, φήσαντος τὸν Ἰακὼβ ἀπαλλασσόμενον τοῦ βίου πεπροφητευκέναι ἑκάστῳ τῶν υἱῶν καὶ τῷ Ἰούδᾳ εἰρηκέναι μετὰ καὶ ἄλλων τό· „οὐκ ἐκλείψει ἄρχων ἐξ Ἰούδα καὶ ἡγούμενος ἐκ τῶν μηρῶν αὐτοῦ, ἕως ἂν ἔλθῃ τὰ ἀποκείμενα αὐτῷ.“ ἐντυγχάνων δέ τις τῇ προφητείᾳ ταύτῃ, κατὰ μὲν τὸ ἀληθὲς πολλῷ πρεσβυτέρᾳ τυγχανούσῃ Μω(??)σέως, ὡς δ᾿ ἂν ὑπονοήσαι τις τῶν οὐ πιστῶν, ὑπὸ Μωϋσέως λεχθείσῃ, θαυμάσαι ἂν, πῶς Μωϋσῆς δεδύνηται προειπεῖν ὅτι οἱ τῶν Ἰουδαίων βασιλεύοντες, δώδεκα οὐσῶν φυλῶν ἐν αὐτοῖς, ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰούδα φυλῆς γεννηθέντες ἄρξουσι τοῦ λαοῦ· διὸ καὶ ὁ πᾶς λαὸς Ἰουδαῖοι ὀνομάζονται, τῆς βασιλευούσης φυλῆς ὄντες ἐπώνυμοι. καὶ δεύτερον δ᾿ ἂν θαυμάσαι τὴν προφητείαν ὁ εὐγνωμόνως αὐτῇ ἐντυγχάνων, τίνα τρόπον εἰπὼν ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰούδα φυλῆς ἔσεσθαι τοὺς ἄρχοντας καὶ ἡγεμόνας τοῦ λαοῦ ἔστησε καὶ τὸ τέλος τῆς ἀρχῆς αὐτῆς εἰπὼν οὐκ ἐκλείψειν ἄρχοντα „ἐξ Ἰούδα“ καὶ ἡγούμενον „ἐκ τῶν μηρῶν αὐτοῦ, ἕως ἂν ἔλθῃ τὰ ἀποκείμενα αὐτῷ, καὶ αὐτὸς προσδοκία ἐθνῶν.“ ἦλθε γὰρ ᾧ ἐστι „τὰ ἀποκείμενα,“ ὁ Χριστὸς τοῦ θεοῦ, „ὁ ἄρχων“ τῶν ἐπαγγελιῶν τοῦ θεοῦ· καὶ σαφῶς γέγονεν οὗτος μόνος παρὰ τοὺς πρὸ αὐτοῦ πάντας, θαῤῥῶν δ᾿ ἂν εἴποιμι καὶ τοὺς μετ᾿ αὐτὸν, „προσδοκία ἐθνῶν“· ἀπὸ γὰρ πάντων τῶν ἐθνῶν πεπιστεύκασι τῷ θεῷ δι᾿ αὐτοῦ, καὶ κατὰ τὸ εἰρημένον ὑπὸ τοῦ Ἡσαΐου ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ ἔθνη ἤλπισαν εἰπόντος· „ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ ἔθνη ἐλπιοῦσιν.“ οὗτος δὲ καὶ εἶπε „τοῖς ἐν δεσμοῖς,“ καθὸ „σειραῖς τῶν ἑαυτοῦ ἁμαρτιῶν ἕκαστος σφίγγεται,“ τὸ „ἐξέλθατε“ καὶ τοῖς ἐν τῇ ἀγνοίᾳ τὸ εἰς φῶς ἥκειν, καὶ τούτων οὕτω προφητευθέντων· „καὶ ἔδωκά σε εἰς διαθήκην ἐθνῶν τοῦ καταστῆσαι τὴν γῆν καὶ κληρονομῆσαι κληρονομίαν ἐρήμου, λέγοντα τοῖς ἐν δεσμοῖς ἐξέλθατε, καὶ τοῖς ἐν σκότει ἀνακαλυφθῆναι.“ καὶ ἔστιν ἰδεῖν ἐπὶ τῇ τούτου παρουσίᾳ διὰ τοὺς πανταχοῦ τῆς οἰκουμένης ἁπλούστερον πιστεύοντας πληρούμενον τὸ „καὶ ἐν πάσαις ταῖς ὁδοῖς βοσκηθήσονται, καὶ ἐν πάσαις ταῖς τρίβοις ἡ νομὴ αὐτῶν.“
pass_a_gloss: If there is need also of a second prophecy appearing to us evident (ἐναργοῦς) about Jesus, we shall set out the one recorded very many years before Jesus' coming by Moses, who said that Jacob, departing life, prophesied to each of his sons and said to Judah among others: 'A ruler (ἄρχων) shall not fail (ἐκλείψει) from Judah nor a leader (ἡγούμενος) from his thighs (μηρῶν), until the things laid up (ἀποκείμενα) for him come.' One reading this prophecy, in truth much older than Moses but, as one of the unbelieving might suspect, spoken by Moses, would wonder how Moses was able to foretell that those reigning of the Jews, there being twelve tribes among them, being born from the tribe of Judah, will rule the people; wherefore also the whole people are named Jews, being named after (ἐπώνυμοι) the reigning tribe. And secondly the one reading it fair-mindedly (εὐγνωμόνως) would wonder at the prophecy, in what manner, having said the rulers and leaders (ἡγεμόνας) of the people would be from the tribe of Judah, he set (ἔστησε) also the end (τέλος) of their rule, saying a ruler will not fail 'from Judah' and a leader 'from his thighs, until the things laid up for him come, and he [is] the expectation (προσδοκία) of the nations.' For he came to whom are 'the things laid up', the Christ of God, 'the ruler' of the promises (ἐπαγγελιῶν) of God; and clearly this one alone beyond (παρά) all those before him, and taking courage (θαρρῶν) I would say also those after him, became 'expectation of nations'; for from all the nations they have believed in God through him, and according to what was said by Isaiah the nations hoped (ἤλπισαν) in his name, he saying: 'In his name nations will hope.' This one also said 'to those in bonds' (δεσμοῖς), inasmuch as 'by the cords (σειραῖς) of his own sins each is bound tight (σφίγγεται)', the 'Come out' (ἐξέλθατε), and to those in ignorance (ἀγνοίᾳ) the coming to light, these things also having been so prophesied: 'And I gave you for a covenant (διαθήκην) of nations to establish (καταστῆσαι) the earth and to inherit an inheritance of desert (ἐρήμου), saying to those in bonds, Come out, and to those in darkness, to be uncovered (ἀνακαλυφθῆναι).' And one can see at his presence (παρουσίᾳ), through those everywhere in the inhabited world believing more simply (ἁπλούστερον), fulfilled the 'And in all the ways they shall be fed (βοσκηθήσονται), and in all the paths their pasture (νομή).'
pass_b_english: And if a second prophecy about Jesus is needed, one that seems to us plain, we shall set out the one written by Moses very many years before Jesus' coming. Moses says that Jacob, as he was departing this life, prophesied to each of his sons (Genesis 49:1), and said to Judah, among other things: "A ruler shall not fail from Judah, nor a leader from his thighs, until the things laid up for him come" (Genesis 49:10).

Anyone who reads this prophecy, which in truth is much older than Moses, though one of the unbelievers might suppose it was spoken by Moses, would wonder how Moses could have foretold that the kings of the Jews, though there were twelve tribes among them, would be born of the tribe of Judah and would rule the people. That is why the whole people are called Jews, taking their name from the ruling tribe.

And one who reads the prophecy fair-mindedly would wonder at it a second time: how, having said that the rulers and leaders of the people would come from the tribe of Judah, he also fixed the end of their rule, saying that a ruler would not fail "from Judah," nor a leader "from his thighs, until the things laid up for him come, and he is the expectation of the nations" (Genesis 49:10). For he has come to whom "the things laid up" belong, the Christ of God, "the ruler" of God's promises. And he alone, beyond all who were before him, and I would boldly say beyond all who came after him too, has clearly become "the expectation of the nations." For people from all the nations have believed in God through him, and, as Isaiah said, the nations have hoped in his name; for he said: "In his name the nations will hope" (Isaiah 42:4).

He also said "Come out" "to those in bonds," since "each one is bound fast by the cords of his own sins" (Proverbs 5:22), and he told those in ignorance to come into the light. These things too were foretold, in this way: "And I have given you as a covenant of the nations, to establish the earth and to inherit a desolate inheritance, saying to those in bonds, Come out, and to those in darkness, Show yourselves" (Isaiah 49:8-9). And at his coming one can see fulfilled, in the simpler believers all over the world, the words: "And in all the ways they shall feed, and in all the paths shall be their pasture" (Isaiah 49:9).

choices.choice: The staged text has Μω(??)σέως twice, read Μωσέως (Moses). Genesis 49:10 is quoted from the Septuagint ('until there come the things laid up for him, and he is the expectation of the nations'), which differs from the Hebrew-based English versions ('until Shiloh come'); the Greek wording is translated. 'Prophesied to each of his sons' paraphrases the setting of Genesis 49:1. 'The ruler' of God's promises picks up ἄρχων from Genesis 49:10. Isaiah 42:4 is the Septuagint wording (also quoted in Matthew 12:21). 'Each one is bound fast by the cords of his own sins' is Proverbs 5:22 in the Septuagint. Isaiah 49:8-9 is quoted from the Septuagint, with κληρονομίαν ἐρήμου (singular) where most witnesses have κληρονομίας ἐρήμους; the sense is unchanged. ἀνακαλυφθῆναι ('to be uncovered') is rendered 'Show yourselves'. The closing quotation is the rest of Isaiah 49:9 (Septuagint). Origen's claim that the prophecy is older than Moses rests on its being Jacob's; no further source is given.
Genesis 49:10: inverted 'until there come the things laid up for him' changed to natural order 'until the things laid up for him come' (both places)
τίνα τρόπον ... ἔστησε: 'for a second reason. Having said ...' restored as the Greek's 'how' clause ('a second time: how, having said ..., he also fixed the end of their rule')
διὰ τοὺς ... ἁπλούστερον πιστεύοντας: 'through the simpler believers' changed to 'in the simpler believers'
Citations checked against the Septuagint: Genesis 49:1, Genesis 49:10, Isaiah 42:4, Proverbs 5:22, Isaiah 49:8-9, Isaiah 49:9
